description.value: Everyone else in the soul economy binds a ghost to a machine and calls it labor. You bind one to yourself, sit down across from it, and negotiate like it still gets a vote — because it does, and it remembers every time you forgot that.

cinderfall.tagline: Everyone else in the soul economy binds a ghost to a machine and calls it labor. You bind one to yourself, sit down across from it, and negotiate like it still gets a vote — because it does, and it remembers every time you forgot that.
cinderfall.role: Negotiator with the Dead — slow trust, sharp debts
terms: Your bound vessel — a corroded saint's mask, a reliquary box wired crooked into your sternum, a conductor's lantern with no bulb left in it. Whatever shape it takes, it's the one thing every wandering soul you've ever struck a deal with has had to move through. Lose it and you lose everything downstream of it.

Your two working states. Quiet is the spirit sitting latent behind the Hollow's seal — you get its patience, its trade-knowledge, its quiet utility. Unveiled is you letting it rise all the way to the surface for a scene — sharper, stronger, and no longer entirely you.

What you owe. Every favor asked of the spirit adds weight to the Toll; every night's rest and honest conversation pays some of it back down. Let it run high enough, or spend past what's fair in a single ask, and the spirit stops being generous about how it collects.

The act of asking — your version of casting a spell. You don't recite words at the dead. You make a case, and the Hollow carries your case to whoever's currently housed inside it. Mechanically this is prepared occult spellcasting: each day you prepare cantrips and spells from the occult list (in What You Learned) and cast them using Wisdom against your Parley DC. Vessel spells and pushing an ask for extra Toll build on top of that base.
What happens when a Parley asks for more than the spirit is willing to give and the Toll can't cover the difference. Never fatal on its own. Never pleasant either.

The setting's word, borrowed by every Hollowbound alive, for the ordinary unhoused dead still wandering the wastes — the raw population you might, with time and risk, talk into the Hollow once your current arrangement runs its course.
